title: Local Frobenius under pullback of constructible rational Weil sheaves
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and let $f:X_0\times_{k_0}k\to Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ be its base change. Use the common-stage rational coefficient categories and constructible Weil sheaves of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and derived pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For every constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $Y_0$, the pullback $Lf^*\mathcal F$, with its induced Weil structure, lies in the constructible heart. Write it as $f^*\mathcal F$. For every closed point $z\in X_0$, the point $x=f_0(z)$ is closed, $\kappa(x)\subset\kappa(z)$ is a finite extension of positive degree $e$, and $q_z=q_x^e$, where $q_t=\#\kappa(t)$. For compatible geometric points there is a natural $\Qlb$-linear isomorphism
$$c_{f,z}:(f^*\mathcal F)_{\bar z}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F_{\bar x},\qquad c_{f,z}F_{z,f^*\mathcal F}=F_{x,\mathcal F}^{\,e}c_{f,z},$$
where the local operators are geometric Frobenius as in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. In particular the eigenvalue multiset at $z$ is $\{\alpha^e:\alpha\in\operatorname{Eig}(F_{x,\mathcal F})\}$, with algebraic multiplicities.

source.place: Step 2, sentence explaining the eigenvalues alpha^e lambda. This is the rational, morphism-functorial input needed there; the cited finite-coefficient trace formula does not itself state it. Compare the concrete realization in WeilConjectures/WeilSheaf/StalkUpperStar.lean:333–358 and StalkCharpoly.lean:588–625; no identification of that concrete category with the common-stage category is assumed.

proof.text: Use zlPull_mem from [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category] to prove the underlying pullback is in the constructible heart. Its carrier is definitionally the actual derived pullback of the original carrier.

Apply [lem-kun-closed-point-field] to z. Its residue field is finite over the finite base field, hence a finite set. The injective residueFieldMap makes the image residue field finite as a set, hence finite over k_0; the converse criterion makes the image point closed. Both residue fields are finite, so the residue extension is finite and has positive finrank. Module.natCard_eq_pow_finrank gives #κ(z)=#κ(x)^e, with e the actual residueDegree.

For compatible geometric lifts use the concrete fdWeilPullbackFibreComparison from [lem-fd-weil-pullback-fibre-return]. Its stated return equation is the required intertwining equation for every Weil sheaf.

The component is a linear isomorphism. Evaluate its intertwining equation at its inverse to identify conjugation of F_z with F_x^e. LinearEquiv.charpoly_conj identifies their characteristic polynomials. Choose an upper triangular basis for F_x using the proved Module.End.exists_basis_isUpperTriangular_toMatrix. Matrix powers stay upper triangular; induction with Matrix.mul_apply shows their diagonal entries are the powers of the original diagonal entries. The proved Matrix.BlockTriangular.charpoly_roots_of_injective identifies roots with this diagonal, with multiplicity. Combining these equations gives exactly the requested multiset power map. The same calculation treats the empty basis and exponent zero.

tool_uses.why: Generic rational/common-stage pullback t-exactness and degree-zero point fibres; a coefficient-category tool, not a replacement of the Fourier argument.
Generic finite-type closed-point residue-field criterion, needed to determine the positive degree of the point extension.
Generic coherent rationalized composition and scalar-extension comparisons, needed to construct the rational stalk isomorphism and its compatibility with the Frobenius square.
Point-fibre scalar extension with identity and tower compatibility, needed to pass the rational comparison to the common-stage fibres.
Naturality of point transport at integral, rational and common-stage coefficients; needed to prove, rather than assume, the Frobenius intertwining.
Normalized rational local point transports and their scalar-extension equation with no finite Tor hypothesis; used as a coefficient tool for the local Frobenius operators.
